Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and a recommended shortlist of models for the pilot/evals you asked for. I focused recommendations on the tradeoffs you mentioned: live chat latency <= 350ms p95, target unit cost < $0.50 per 1k tokens, and preserving answer quality for short-form support responses (~1–3 sentences).

Top recommended models (shortlist and rationale):

1) redwood-2-mini (8-bit) — Low cost, very low latency
   - Why: ~30–50ms token latency on our 4xA10s in reserved mode; best for high-volume real-time chat.
   - Tradeoff: Quality is good for short Q/A but may hallucinate on complex multi-step reasoning.
   - Use-case: Live support suggestions, quick completions, initial ranking before a higher-quality model.

2) redwood-2-medium-8bit — Balanced quality & cost
   - Why: Solid step-up in answer accuracy with modest latency (~80–120ms token latency).
   - Tradeoff: Higher cost (~2–3x mini) but noticeably better coherence on follow-ups.
   - Use-case: Primary candidate for pilot when quality matters for user satisfaction.

3) open-13b-q8 (quantized) — High quality, moderate latency/cost
   - Why: Best end-to-end accuracy in our benchmarks for your prompt set, especially on multi-turn context.
   - Tradeoff: Latency ~150–300ms token; cost higher but still much cheaper than top-tier large models.
   - Use-case: Escalation path for tickets flagged as critical or for quality-sensitive flows.

Suggested pilot design (quick):
- 1-week A/B eval across the three models above using your support prompt set (~500 prompts).
- Measure: p95 latency (route time + token), token cost per response, precision@1 on labeled prompts, and human-rated quality on 100 sampled replies.
- Success criteria: redwood-2-medium-8bit meets precision target with p95 <= 350ms and cost <= $0.75 per 1k tokens.

Attachments & links: I attached a short benchmark summary (acme-benchmark-summary.pdf) and uploaded full per-model logs/CSV + prompt sets here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-acme-evals

Next steps / ask:
- Approve the 1-week eval (we'll provision a dedicated pilot pool and ingest your 500 prompts).
- Share any additional prompt variants you want included (we included the prompt-set in the Drive link).
- If agreed, I'll schedule a 30-min checkpoint after 3 days to sync results and decide whether to narrow to two models.

I'll loop in Dev for bench-level numbers and the suggested eval config.

Best,

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Quick answers and a bit more detail on the eval config we recommend.

1) Regression detection / alerts - Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against your baseline prompt set. You can configure:
   - Baseline (we'll capture precision@1 on first run).
   - Daily auto-eval on incoming prompt stream or synthetic replay.
   - Alerting: configurable thresholds (e.g., precision drop >5% OR human-rated quality delta >0.3) that create tickets / webhook notifications.
   - We also provide diffed examples (before/after) for triage.

2) Ballpark pricing (hosted per 1M input+output tokens) — approximate published/hosted list prices for pilot sizing:
   - redwood-2-mini: $12 / 1M tokens
   - redwood-2-medium-8bit: $36 / 1M tokens
   - open-13b-q8: $68 / 1M tokens
   Notes: Dedicated reserved pools will reduce unit cost by ~30–50% depending on commit.

3) Benchmarks (summary numbers from the attached CSV):
   - redwood-2-mini: p95 end-to-end per-response latency ~220ms (chat-turn), median token latency ~35ms, avg cost per response on your sample ~ $0.003
   - redwood-2-medium-8bit: p95 ~310ms, median token latency ~85ms, avg cost per response ~ $0.009
   - open-13b-q8: p95 ~460ms, median token latency ~150ms, avg cost per response ~ $0.022

4) Suggested eval config (we'll provision a 4-GPU reserved pool for the week):
   - Prompt set: 500 production prompts + 100 adversarial prompts (edge cases) — attached model-eval-prompt-set.json
   - Metrics: precision@1, p95 latency, token cost, hallucination rate (auto-check + human review on 100 samples)
   - Monitoring: webhook on threshold breach + daily summary email + shared CSV in drive

Attachments uploaded: model-eval-prompt-set.json, benchmark-results.csv (full logs). Live Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-acme-evals (same as Marissa's link).

Security / compliance: Marissa already shared pilot scope with your security team; we can provide SOC2 Type II report and configure data retention = 30 days for pilot. If you need a private VPC pilot, we can discuss Dedicated/Private options — that requires a short procurement path.

If this looks good I can kick off provisioning as soon as you confirm.

Thanks,
